mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the risk-free rate, increasing the present value of equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The signal is active whenever FEDFUNDS is below a historical threshold of 3.0%.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 3.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when UNRATE > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue growth expectations and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% from the previous month, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) leads to higher real interest rates and reduced equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.1% in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1300.0 thousand units signals weak consumer demand for housing, reducing construction activity and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when HOUST < 1300.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock (INDPRO decline > 1.0% in 3 months), a simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals stagflation, reducing corporate profit margins and driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when INDPRO declines > 1.0% in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
